name: Fragrance signature scent

lead: A signature scent is one fragrance worn consistently so others link it with you, making your personal image more memorable. Communities treat it as a memorability and personal-branding tool.

Repeated exposure is said to build the association between a smell and a person. Perfume references cite long-running classics such as Chanel No. 5 and Guerlain's Shalimar, and list fragrance families including floral, amber, woody, fougere and fresh. No studies on social effects were found.

paras: People choose a fragrance, often within a family they like, and wear it every day, adjusting strength by concentration such as parfum, eau de parfum or eau de toilette.
Fragrance ingredients can be allergenic; no studies on social effects were found.

chain: Others link the scent to you
angle.text: Users adopt a single signature fragrance so others come to associate the scent with them, building a more memorable personal image. The idea is popular in appearance communities.

lead: A signature scent is a single fragrance a person wears consistently so that others come to associate it with them. In appearance communities it is discussed as a memorability and personal-branding tool.

Perfume references cite many long-running fragrances, such as Chanel No. 5 and Guerlain's Shalimar, as classics.[1] Fragrance families include floral, amber, woody, fougere and fresh,[1] and concentration labels (parfum, eau de parfum, eau de toilette) vary in strength between brands.[1] No studies of signature scents and social perception were found.

paras: Typical longevity is about 2 to 4 hours for eau de toilette and up to 6 to 8 for perfume.[1] Wearers pick a fragrance family that suits them and use it daily.
Perfume materials can include allergenic compounds.[1]

lore.intro: Signature scents are discussed as a way to be remembered.

claims.claim: A consistent signature scent makes you memorable
